difficultyRationale: Tests recall of the precise definition of DRY, which is a common point of confusion when distinguished from mere textual similarity.
prompt: What does the DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) principle most precisely refer to avoiding?
explanation: DRY is about a single piece of knowledge or business decision having one authoritative representation in the system. The risk it guards against is that the knowledge changes in one place while a duplicate of it is left unchanged, not that two pieces of code happen to look alike.

options.text: Writing two pieces of code that happen to look similar, even if they represent unrelated decisions made by different parts of the business, such as a marketing rule and a shipping rule that currently use the same numeric thresholds by pure coincidence.
options.explanation: Surface-level textual similarity is not what DRY targets; two blocks of code can look identical while encoding different knowledge, in which case unifying them would be a mistake, not a DRY fix.

options.text: Using a loop instead of writing out repeated statements by hand.
options.explanation: This describes a coding-style choice about iteration constructs, not the duplicated-knowledge concern that DRY addresses; DRY applies at the level of business or design decisions, not just syntactic repetition of statements.

options.text: Repeating the same piece of knowledge or business decision in multiple places in the system, so that a single conceptual change requires finding and updating every copy.
options.explanation: DRY is about a single piece of knowledge having one authoritative representation; the risk being guarded against is that one decision changes while a duplicate of it is forgotten, which is exactly the failure mode Fowler's writing on repetition targets.

options.text: Calling the same method more than once within a single function.
options.explanation: Calling a method multiple times is normal program behavior, not duplication of knowledge; DRY is not about limiting how often existing, correctly shared logic is invoked.
